prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1321; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a side impact at a controlled intersection. The insured driver is named on the policy, and the claimant was identified at the scene as a passenger in the vehicle that was struck. Police report and witness statements place the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the collision.

Entry 2: Claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office. Photographs taken at the scene confirm several visible details of the impact. No independent witnesses have been located beyond the parties and responding officers.

Entry 3: Vehicle damage was reviewed and is mostly consistent with the described side impact and direction of force. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior records, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 4: Reported wrist fracture was reviewed against the mechanism of this crash and is plausible. Medical records show a prior minor strain to the same area several years ago, which healed fully and has been noted for completeness.

Entry 5: Treatment followed a typical course, with imaging, immobilization, and therapy, and the claimant's symptoms and treatment intensity tapered as recovery progressed. The claimant has given the same account of the collision in every conversation to date.

Entry 6: File remains open pending receipt of final treatment summary and the attorney's itemized documentation. Reserve reviewed and no change recommended at this time.
